note.question: Can making knowledge sharing require prior individual learning reduce free riding and increase an organization's total knowledge?
note.overview: Group members simultaneously allocate time between costly individual learning and social learning, creating a knowledge-production externality; the paper derives unique symmetric Nash equilibria and evolutionary stability.

components.label: Unique symmetric Nash equilibrium and evolutionarily stable strategy
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique symmetric Nash equilibrium and evolutionarily stable strategy. Without absorptive capacity, Theorem 1 on printed/PDF p. 6 gives q^e=w/[theta(n-1)] and payoff w. Under Assumptions 1-3, Theorem 2 on printed/PDF p. 9 proves a unique symmetric interior pure-strategy equilibrium with payoff above w and greater available knowledge; both equilibria are evolutionarily stable.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Members simultaneously choose the fraction of time devoted to individual learning; remaining time is spent learning from others. Individual learning creates knowledge spillovers, and absorptive capacity determines how much of others' knowledge each member can use. Individual learning creates a positive externality but competes for time with social learning. Absorptive capacity links own contribution to the private return from others' contributions.
